lead: `echo` of a `float` prints the way PHP's default precision does, so an example cannot show float inexactness by printing one.
body: `Core\Arr::sum([0.1, 0.2])` prints `0.3` rather than `0.30000000000000004`, and a comment promising the long digits is wrong the moment `--bless` writes the `.out`. Show the difference with a comparison — `Core\Arr::sum($shares) == 0.3 ? 'yes' : 'no'` prints `no` — which is what `docs/examples/lang/expressions/arithmetic/03-a-basket-priced-in-decimal.nvs` already does.
